title: Categorizing Inharmonicity — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Categorizing Inharmonicity's rich face, its first round, a Study and still a proposal: two walks that each start from one idea and end on a measurement (where each kind of inharmonicity leaves the harmonic series for the person listening, on one ruler for all six; and whether phase alone can make a tone inharmonic, which it can, but only in a loop, and what it makes there is the stretch), beside the page's own May proofs, gathered as they were and captioned with what was measured on them. I grow when the page is enriched again; I never hold the entry's words.

offers.what: § 6's synthesis list says to feed a harmonic tone through the all-pass cascade and that 'the output spectrum is inharmonic even though the input was harmonic'. Measured on the phase-loop piece's engine: through the cascade once, no partial of a harmonic tone moves (0.0000 ¢ over sixteen partials, M = 4 to 16, a = −0.85 to 0.5; energy in ÷ out 1.0000). A fixed filter can't make a frequency that wasn't there. It takes the cascade inside a delay loop, as the section's first sentence says: then partial 16 sits +48.75 ¢ off its ghost (M = 8, a = −0.6), within 0.08 ¢ of where ω·D + M·φ(ω) = 2πk predicts. Proposed: 'Put the cascade inside a delay loop and pluck it; the loop's modes are inharmonic though nothing in it changes level', in place of feeding a tone through.

§ 6's signature φ(f) = α·f + β·f² + …: only the part beyond α·f bends the spacing. α·f is plain delay; it retunes the loop and keeps it harmonic (the straight-line-phase control of the same low-frequency length sits within 0.11 ¢ of whole-number places). And what a fixed first-order cascade makes is § 1's pattern: the stiff-string formula fits the loop's sixteen partials to 1.22 ¢ rms (M = 8, a = −0.6, B = 2.31 × 10⁻⁴), drifting off it only at extreme settings (24.9 ¢ rms at M = 4, a = −0.85). This is how waveguide pianos model stiffness (Van Duyne and Smith, 1994). So phase accumulation reads as a pathway to the stretch rather than a pattern of its own, and its 'ghostly … slowly evolving' character needs the coefficients to move; a fixed chain gives a fixed tone.

§ 4: 'logarithmic in their frequency (or equivalently, proportional to the partial number)' — the two are not equivalent; log n is not n. What the formula f_n = n·f₀·(1 + B·log n) gives, for small B, is almost exactly f₀·n^(1+B) (within 0.65 ¢ over sixteen partials at B = 0.01, 2.57 ¢ at 0.02): the same stretch for every doubling of partial number (23.8, 23.5, 23.2, 22.9 ¢ per octave at 0.02), a stretched octave. The section's B is also a different quantity from § 1's B under the same letter; b would keep them apart.

§ 2: a drumhead's rim holds still, ψ = 0, so its modes sit at zeros of J_m, which are the J₀ and J₁ lists the section gives (checked numerically). The condition the section names, ∂ψ/∂r = 0, is a free rim, whose radial modes sit at zeros of J₀′ = −J₁ (3.832, 7.016 …). Found in reading, not by a piece: cymbals and tam-tams are plates, not membranes; their bending waves put frequency with k², not k, so their partials are not these zeros.

§ 2: 'The spacing is not uniform' — within one family it nearly is. Consecutive zeros of J₀ differ by 3.115, 3.134, 3.138, 3.139 … tending to π; the gathered Bessel proof's partials are 285 to 287 Hz apart above the first. One family is a harmonic comb slid up (partial n at about π·(n − ¼)), levelling near +463 ¢ against the harmonic places. The non-uniform, bell-like spacing comes from several families (m = 0, 1, 2 …) sounding together.

The opening holds that the types are different kinds, not degrees. Set to the same mistuning on one ruler (loudness-weighted RMS cents), their patterns of partials measured: at 10 ¢, stretched and the phase loop are 0.96 ¢ apart, Bessel and logarithmic 2.38 ¢, every other pair 6.8 to 14.8 ¢ (at 25 ¢: 3.49, 5.86, and 14 to 37). By pattern the six are about four; chaotic and stochastic differ from each other mainly in that one moves and one is frozen. The list mixes mechanisms (stiffness, an all-pass loop, chaos, chance) with patterns (stretched, logarithmic, Bessel). Whether each gap is heard is the reader's test in the threshold piece's step 3; the gaps here are measured, the hearing isn't.

Under Perceptual threshold, a pointer like the Kuramoto question's: the rich face now asks it of each listener, blind (two tones, which one left; a 2-down 1-up staircase, about thirty rounds a kind), on one ruler for all six kinds. The question as written assumes a common magnitude that the palette's 'magnitude slider 0 = perfectly harmonic, 1 = maximum deviation' doesn't define; the face's ruler is loudness-weighted RMS cents, and a ruler that counted the farthest partial would rank the kinds differently.

pieces.title: five flavours · the May spectrograms
pieces.caption: **The May proofs, side by side.** Spectrograms of a harmonic reference and four kinds at 220 Hz, sixteen partials, the first second of each. Measured on the sound files beside it: stretched is B = 0.0008; Bessel is the J₀ family scaled so partial 1 is 220 Hz; stochastic moved partial 1 too, to 229 Hz; chaotic is a frozen scatter. No proof for logarithmic or phase accumulation; the two pieces in this section play all six.
pieces.near: Inharmonic partial deviations lie in a multidimensional space

pieces.by: the Maker · Web Audio, rendered buffers
pieces.title: when does it leave? · a walk in four steps
pieces.caption: **When does each kind leave the harmonic series, and is it the same for every kind?** The page's open threshold question, asked of you. The harmonic series alone, with one ruler for all six kinds (loudness-weighted RMS cents); one kind raised from zero, with a sighted mark; all six set to the same mistuning, where stretched and the phase loop land about a tenth of it apart and Bessel and logarithmic about a quarter; and last a blind two-tone staircase that finds your threshold for each kind and compares them. The engine was checked headless: a simulated listener's threshold comes back within 2%. What a person hears was not checked.
pieces.near: Inharmonic partial deviations lie in a multidimensional space

pieces.title: harmonic · May proof
pieces.caption: **Harmonic, the reference.** 220 Hz, sixteen partials on their whole-number places, a 4 s fall.
pieces.near: Inharmonic partial deviations lie in a multidimensional space

pieces.title: stretched · May proof
pieces.caption: **Stretched.** B = 0.0008, measured on the file: partial 16 at 3863.7 Hz against a ghost at 3520, 162 ¢ sharp. f₀ is 220 Hz and not pinned, so partial 1 sits at 220.09.
pieces.near: The most familiar form: partials sharpen progressively

pieces.title: Bessel · May proof
pieces.caption: **Bessel.** The zeros of J₀ scaled so the first is 220 Hz: 505.0, 791.7, 1078.7 Hz and up. One family, so above the first gap the spacing is almost even, about 287 Hz: a comb slid up rather than a stretch. A real drumhead sounds many families at once.

pieces.title: stochastic · May proof
pieces.caption: **Stochastic.** Every partial scattered by up to about 60 Hz, the first included (to 229.1 Hz), and fixed for the whole note.
pieces.near: Partials deviate from harmonic positions by random amounts

pieces.title: chaotic · May proof
pieces.caption: **Chaotic, as rendered in May.** Scattered, not moving: the same partials in its first and second seconds, and nothing below 220 Hz, so no period-doubling. By ear it is a second stochastic proof. The threshold piece's chaotic kind is the one that moves while it sounds.
pieces.near: When a physical oscillator is driven beyond a critical amplitude

pieces.by: the Maker · a loop rendered sample by sample, measured by FFT
pieces.title: phase only, in a loop · a walk in four steps
pieces.caption: **Can phase alone make a tone inharmonic?** § 6's claim, measured on the sound. A loop that only delays rings harmonic; the same all-passes outside the loop move no partial; inside it they put partial 16 about 49 ¢ sharp at the start setting, while a straight-line-phase control of the same length stays within 0.11 ¢, and the stiff-string formula fits the loop's sixteen partials to about 1.2 ¢. So yes, entirely phase, but only in a loop, and what it makes is the stretch. Every number was checked headless; the sound was not listened to.
pieces.near: The output spectrum is inharmonic even though the input was harmonic
